holidays.name: Embrace Your Geekness Day
holidays.description: Today is for letting your inner nerd out. Whether you love sci-fi marathons, tabletop RPGs, coding, anime or train timetables, you're encouraged to share it loudly and without apology. Geek out, gush, and cheer on other people's obsessions too.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a popular pop-culture holiday that celebrates passionate enthusiasm for any niche interest.
holidays.funFact: The word 'geek' comes from the Low German word 'geck', which meant a fool. It has since gone from an insult to a badge of honor.

holidays.name: National Beans 'n' Franks Day
holidays.description: This day honors a humble, budget-friendly comfort food. It pairs sweet, smoky baked beans with sliced hot dogs. It's a cookout and camping favorite that turns up at summer picnics and in kids' lunchboxes.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It falls in the middle of summer cookout season, when the dish is at its most popular.
holidays.funFact: Baked beans have a long history in American cooking, particularly in New England. Adding sliced franks turned a traditional side dish into a quick one-pot meal.

holidays.name: National Barbershop Music Appreciation Day
holidays.description: This day celebrates close-harmony, four-part singing, performed a cappella with no instruments. Barbershop music is known for its ringing chords and tight blends. Today is a good excuse to find a quartet and listen, or to gather some friends and try singing it yourself.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It honors the American vocal tradition that grew in popularity in the late 1800s and early 1900s and is still performed today by quartets and choruses.
holidays.funFact: The Barbershop Harmony Society, one of the biggest groups dedicated to the style, was founded in Tulsa, Oklahoma, in 1938.
